content.content:
An integer type coerces from each other integer type all of whose values it holds,
as listed above; every other conversion between integer types is written explicitly.

Among the explicit conversions, the method \VAR{narrow} converts a value of
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}64} or \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} to \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, and a value of
\EXP{\mathbb{N}64} to \EXP{\mathbb{N}32}, by keeping its low 32 bits: the result
is the value of the narrower type that is congruent to the argument modulo
\EXP{2^{32}}.
A value that the narrower type holds is unchanged; any other wraps, and no
\TYP{IntegerOverflow} is thrown.

The operators \OPR{LSHIFT} and \OPR{RSHIFT} shift the bits of an integer of any of
the five types by a count of any integer type, and return a value of the type of
the integer shifted.
On \EXP{\mathbb{Z}}, \EXP{x \OPR{LSHIFT} k} is \EXP{\VAR{shift}(x,k)} and
and \EXP{/} is subtle.
\See{operator-precedence} for a discussion of the relative precedence of
these operations and how precedence may depend on the use of whitespace.

The handling of overflow depends on the type of the number produced.
For integer results, overflow throws an \TYP{IntegerOverflow}.
Rational computations do not overflow.
For floating-point results, overflow produces \EXP{+\infty} or \EXP{-\infty}
according to the rules of IEEE 754.
For intervals, overflow produces an appropriate containing interval.

Underflow is relevant only to floating-point computations and is handled
according to the rules of IEEE 754.

The handling of division by zero depends on the type of the number produced.
For integer results, division by zero throws a \TYP{DivisionByZero}.
For rational results, division by zero produces \EXP{1/0}.
\subsection{Addition and Subtraction Operators}

Addition and subtraction are expressed with \EXP{+} and \EXP{-} on all numeric quantities,
including intervals, as well as vectors and matrices.

The handling of overflow depends on the type of the number produced.
For integer results, overflow throws an \TYP{IntegerOverflow}.
Rational computations do not overflow.
For floating-point results, overflow produces \EXP{+\infty} or \EXP{-\infty}
according to the rules of IEEE 754.
For intervals, overflow produces an appropriate containing interval.

Underflow is relevant only to floating-point computations and is handled
according to the rules of IEEE 754.

Wraparound addition and subtraction on fixed-size integers are
expressed by \EXP{\dotplus} and \EXP{\dotminus}.
Saturating addition and subtraction on fixed-size integers are
expressed by \EXP{\boxplus} and \EXP{\boxminus}.
These operations do not overflow.

Ordinary addition and subtraction of floating-point numbers always
use the IEEE 754 ``round to nearest'' rounding mode.  This rounding
mode may be emphasized by using the operators \EXP{\oplus}
and \EXP{\ominus}.  Addition and subtraction in ``round toward zero''
mode may be expressed with \EXP{\boxplus} and \EXP{\boxminus}.
Addition and subtraction in ``round toward positive infinity''
mode may be expressed with \EXP{\upplus} and \EXP{\upminus}.
Addition and subtraction in ``round toward negative infinity''
mode may be expressed with \EXP{\downplus} and \EXP{\downminus}.

The construction \EXP{x \pm y} produces the interval \EXP{\bsINT{x-y,x+y}}.

\subsection{Intersection, Union, and Set Difference Operators}

Sets support the operations of intersection \EXP{\cap}, union
\EXP{\cup}, disjoint union \EXP{\uplus},
set difference \EXP{\setminus}, and symmetric set difference
\EXP{\ominus}.  Disjoint union
throws \TYP{DisjointUnionError} if the arguments are in fact not disjoint.

(* NN32's operators and getters bound to nativeHelpers keep their values, their wraparound and their IntegerOverflow under walk. *)
component NativeHelperFamilyNN32Walk
export Executable

overflows(f: () -> NN32): Boolean =
  try
    f()
    false
  catch e
    IntegerOverflow => true
  end

run():() = do
  m: ZZ32 = -1
  lo: ZZ32 = -2147483647 - 1
  n0 = unsigned(0)
  n1 = unsigned(1)
  n7 = unsigned(7)
  n16 = unsigned(65536)
  n31 = unsigned(lo)
  nmax = unsigned(m)
  assert(n0.asString, "0", "asString of 0")
  assert(n7.asString, "7", "asString of 7")
  assert(n16.asString, "65536", "asString of 2^16")
  assert(n31.asString, "2147483648", "asString of 2^31")
  assert(nmax.asString, "4294967295", "asString of 2^32-1")
  assert(n7.asExprString, "7", "asExprString of 7")
  assert(n31.asExprString, "2147483648", "asExprString of 2^31")
  assert(nmax.asExprString, "4294967295", "asExprString of 2^32-1")
  assert(n7 = unsigned(7), true, "=")
  assert(nmax = nmax, true, "= of 2^32-1")
  assert(nmax = n31, false, "= unequal")
  assert(n0 = n7, false, "= unequal at 0")
  assert(n7 < n16, true, "<")
  assert(n31 < nmax, true, "< above the signed half")
  assert(nmax < n7, false, "< is unsigned")
  assert(n7 < n31, true, "< below and above the signed half")
  assert(n0 < n0, false, "< not")
  assert((-n0).asString, "0", "unary - of 0")
  assert(overflows(fn () => -n7), "unary - of 7 overflows")
  assert(overflows(fn () => -nmax), "unary - of 2^32-1 overflows")
  assert((DOTMINUS n0).asString, "0", "unary DOTMINUS of 0")
  assert((DOTMINUS n7).asString, "4294967289", "unary DOTMINUS of 7 wraps")
  assert((DOTMINUS n31).asString, "2147483648", "unary DOTMINUS of 2^31 wraps")
  assert((DOTMINUS nmax).asString, "1", "unary DOTMINUS of 2^32-1 wraps")
  assert((n7 + n7).asString, "14", "+")
  assert((n31 + n16).asString, "2147549184", "+ past the signed half")
  assert((nmax + n0).asString, "4294967295", "+ of 0")
  assert(overflows(fn () => nmax + n7), "+ overflows")
  assert(overflows(fn () => n31 + n31), "+ at 2^32 overflows")
  assert((n7 DOTPLUS n7).asString, "14", "DOTPLUS")
  assert((nmax DOTPLUS n7).asString, "6", "DOTPLUS wraps")
  assert((n31 DOTPLUS n31).asString, "0", "DOTPLUS wraps at 2^32")
  assert((nmax - n7).asString, "4294967288", "-")
  assert((n7 - n7).asString, "0", "- to 0")
  assert(overflows(fn () => n0 - n7), "- below 0 overflows")
  assert(overflows(fn () => n7 - nmax), "- of 2^32-1 overflows")
  assert((n16 DOTMINUS n7).asString, "65529", "DOTMINUS")
  assert((n0 DOTMINUS n7).asString, "4294967289", "DOTMINUS wraps")
  assert((n7 DOTMINUS nmax).asString, "8", "DOTMINUS of 2^32-1 wraps")
  assert((n16 DOT n7).asString, "458752", "DOT")
  assert(overflows(fn () => n16 DOT n16), "DOT at 2^32 overflows")
  assert(overflows(fn () => nmax DOT n7), "DOT overflows")
  assert((n7 TIMES n7).asString, "49", "TIMES")
  assert((n31 TIMES n1).asString, "2147483648", "TIMES by 1")
  assert(overflows(fn () => n16 TIMES n16), "TIMES at 2^32 overflows")
  assert(overflows(fn () => n31 TIMES n7), "TIMES overflows")
  j = n7 n16
  assert(j.asString, "458752", "juxtaposition")
  assert(overflows(fn () => n16 n16), "juxtaposition at 2^32 overflows")
  assert((n16 DOTTIMES n16).asString, "0", "DOTTIMES wraps at 2^32")
  assert((nmax DOTTIMES nmax).asString, "1", "DOTTIMES of 2^32-1 wraps")
  assert((nmax DOTTIMES n7).asString, "4294967289", "DOTTIMES wraps")
  assert((n16 DOTTIMES n7).asString, "458752", "DOTTIMES")
  assert((nmax DIV n7).asString, "613566756", "DIV is unsigned")
  assert((n31 DIV n16).asString, "32768", "DIV of 2^31")
  assert((n7 DIV nmax).asString, "0", "DIV by 2^32-1")
  assert((nmax DIV nmax).asString, "1", "DIV of 2^32-1 by itself")
  assert((nmax BITAND n7).asString, "7", "BITAND")
  assert((n31 BITAND nmax).asString, "2147483648", "BITAND of 2^31")

  assert((BITNOT n0).asString, "4294967295", "BITNOT of 0")
  assert((BITNOT n31).asString, "2147483647", "BITNOT of 2^31")
  assert((BITNOT nmax).asString, "0", "BITNOT of 2^32-1")
  assert(widen(n0).asString, "0", "widen of 0")
  assert(widen(n7).asString, "7", "widen of 7")
  assert(widen(n31).asString, "2147483648", "widen of 2^31")
  assert(widen(nmax).asString, "4294967295", "widen of 2^32-1")

component NN32DivisionByZeroWalk
export Executable

dividesByZero(f: () -> NN32): Boolean =
  try
    f()
    false
  catch e
    DivisionByZero => true
  end

  assert(dividesByZero(fn () => unsigned(7) DIV unsigned(0)), "NN32 7 DIV 0 throws DivisionByZero; opr-overview.tex, section \"Multiplication, Division, Modulo, and Remainder Operators\"")
  assert((unsigned(7) DIV unsigned(2)).asString, "3", "NN32 7 DIV 2 is 3")
  println("NN32 DIV by zero: DivisionByZero")
end

end

component IntSemanticsRungB
import java com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.{simpleIntArith.intSaturatingDiv => jIntSaturatingDiv,
                                            simpleIntArith.intSaturatingAbs => jIntSaturatingAbs,
                                            simpleLongArith.longSaturatingDiv => jLongSaturatingDiv,
                                            simpleLongArith.longSaturatingAbs => jLongSaturatingAbs}
export Executable

(*) explorations/compile-ladder/rung-int-semantics-compiled/REPORT.md

shouldOverflow32(f: () -> ZZ32): Boolean =
  try
    ignore f()
    false
  catch e
    IntegerOverflow => true
    Exception => false
  end

shouldOverflow64(f: () -> ZZ64): Boolean =
  try
    ignore f()
    false
  catch e
    IntegerOverflow => true
    Exception => false
  end

run(): () = do
  zero: ZZ32 = 0
  one: ZZ32 = 1
  two: ZZ32 = 2
  three: ZZ32 = 3
  five: ZZ32 = 5
  mOne: ZZ32 = -1
  mTwo: ZZ32 = -2
  mThree: ZZ32 = -3
  mSixteen: ZZ32 = -16
  thirtyOne: ZZ32 = 31
  thirtyTwo: ZZ32 = 32
  thirtyThree: ZZ32 = 33
  mForty: ZZ32 = -40
  zMax: ZZ32 = 7FFFFFFF_16
  zMin: ZZ32 = -zMax - 1

  assert((three LSHIFT thirtyOne).asString, "-2147483648", "row 335: ZZ32 3 LSHIFT 31")
  assert((three LSHIFT thirtyTwo).asString, "0", "row 335: ZZ32 3 LSHIFT 32")
  assert((three LSHIFT thirtyThree).asString, "0", "row 335: ZZ32 3 LSHIFT 33")
  assert((three RSHIFT thirtyThree).asString, "0", "row 335: ZZ32 3 RSHIFT 33")
  assert((mSixteen RSHIFT thirtyTwo).asString, "-1", "row 335: ZZ32 -16 RSHIFT 32")
  assert((mSixteen RSHIFT thirtyThree).asString, "-1", "row 335: ZZ32 -16 RSHIFT 33")
  assert((three LSHIFT mOne).asString, "1", "row 335: ZZ32 3 LSHIFT -1")
  assert((three RSHIFT mOne).asString, "6", "row 335: ZZ32 3 RSHIFT -1")
  assert((mSixteen LSHIFT mTwo).asString, "-4", "row 335: ZZ32 -16 LSHIFT -2")
  assert((mSixteen LSHIFT mForty).asString, "-1", "row 335: ZZ32 -16 LSHIFT -40")
  assert((three RSHIFT mForty).asString, "0", "row 335: ZZ32 3 RSHIFT -40")
  assert((three LSHIFT zMin).asString, "0", "row 335: ZZ32 3 LSHIFT MIN")
  assert((mThree LSHIFT zMin).asString, "-1", "row 335: ZZ32 -3 LSHIFT MIN")
  assert((three RSHIFT zMin).asString, "0", "row 335: ZZ32 3 RSHIFT MIN")

  threeL: ZZ64 = 3
tests=IntSemanticsRungB
link
run

  assert(n32ToString(n32WrapMul(nmax, n7)) = "4294967289", "WrapMul wraps")

# which runs the gate's compiled tracks. The JVMs keep their temporary files, parser directories among them,
# in the tree's tmp/.
export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64
export PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH"
export FORTRESS_HOME="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../../../.." && pwd)"
unset JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS
export FORTRESS_THREADS=4
mkdir -p "$FORTRESS_HOME/tmp"
export JAVA_FLAGS="-Xmx4g -Xss64m -Djava.io.tmpdir=$FORTRESS_HOME/tmp"
FH=$FORTRESS_HOME; L=${1:?label}; D=$(cd "${2:?dir}" && pwd); shift 2
cd "$FH/ProjectFortress"
CP=$(../bin/fortress_classpath | tail -1)
echo "# junit.sh $L $(date -u +%FT%TZ); nproc $(nproc); $(grep -m1 'model name' /proc/cpuinfo | cut -d: -f2 | sed 's/^ //'); $(grep -m1 'cpu MHz' /proc/cpuinfo | cut -d: -f2 | sed 's/^ //') MHz; load at start $(cut -d' ' -f1-3 /proc/loadavg); $(java -version 2>&1 | head -1); FORTRESS_THREADS=$FORTRESS_THREADS; tree $(git -C $FH rev-parse --short HEAD)$(git -C $FH diff --quiet HEAD -- ProjectFortress Library || echo ' with the next rung applied, not yet committed'); tests from $D"
clean () { for t in "$@"; do n=$(sed -n 's/^tests=//p' "$D/$t" | head -1); [ -n "$n" ] && find ../default_repository/caches -name "*$n*" -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null; done; }
clean "$@"
if [ -n "${ONE_JVM:-}" ]; then
  files=(); for t in "$@"; do files+=("$D/$t"); done
  echo "########## [$L] fortress junit, one JVM: $*"
  java $JAVA_FLAGS -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 -cp "$CP" com.sun.fortress.Shell junit "${files[@]}" 2>&1 | sed "s#$FH/##g" | grep -v '^\s*at ' | cut -c1-240
  echo "exit=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
else
for t in "$@"; do
  echo "########## [$L] fortress junit $t"
  java $JAVA_FLAGS -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 -cp "$CP" com.sun.fortress.Shell junit "$D/$t" 2>&1 | sed "s#$FH/##g" | grep -v '^\s*at ' | cut -c1-240
  echo "exit=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
done
fi
clean "$@"

== explorations/coordinator/map/modules-and-phases.md:441-455

## B.12 Native code and Java interop

The two worlds bind native code by two mechanisms that share nothing but the word "native".

Interpreter: a function whose body is literally `builtinPrimitive("some.java.Class")` is pattern-matched in `NativeApp.checkAndLoadNative` (`interpreter/glue/NativeApp.java:164-223`). A string under `com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.` names a static Java method, `"com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.Class.method"`: `interpreter/glue/StaticNativeApp.java` takes, among the class's public static methods of that name, the one whose Java types carry the declared types, `self` first, and calls it by reflection, each argument unboxed and the result boxed (`NativeApp.java:194-201`; since rung W, `640acb4a1`; F-299). Any other string names a class — a subclass of `NativeFn0..3`/`NativeMeth0..3` in `interpreter/glue/` — which is loaded reflectively and takes the evaluator's boxed `FValue`s directly.

There are 231 such bindings in `LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss`, 108 in `Library/FortressLibrary.fss` and 7 in `LibraryBuiltin/NativeArray.fss`.

Compiler: a `.fss` writes `import java com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.{class.method => name, …}` (16 such lines in `LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss`, 3 in `Library/CompilerLibrary.fss`); `ForeignJava` reads the Java class with ASM to synthesize an api for it (`repository/ForeignJava.java:132-136,565-575`), and `FortressTransformer` rewrites the class into a wrapper whose methods take and return the compiled world's boxed values (`compiler/nativeInterface/FortressTransformer.java:37`, wrapper written to `nativewrapper_cache` at `:33`).

`import java` also works on the interpreter path, by a third route that is easy to miss: `ForeignComponentWrapper` populates an environment from `ForeignJava`'s synthesized declarations (`interpreter/env/ForeignComponentWrapper.java:59`), and `ClosureMaker` generates, at run time, a `NativeFn<n>` subclass that calls the Java method and writes it into `bytecode_cache` (`interpreter/env/ClosureMaker.java:44-50,52`).

No test under `ProjectFortress/tests/` uses `import java` (0 files), while 2 under `compiler_tests/` do, so the interpreter's foreign-Java route is present but not exercised by the gated suite.

There is no way for a Fortress program to be called *from* Java other than by loading the generated classes through `InstantiatingClassloader`, which is what `MainWrapper` does.

/**
 * The compiled path's reading of a native binding.  A declaration whose body is
 * exactly builtinPrimitive("pkg.Class.method"), the tight juxtaposition that walk's
 * NativeApp.checkAndLoadNative recognizes, where the string names a public static
 * method of a class of the helpers' package, com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers., becomes
 * a call of that method through the import java machinery: the component gains
 * import java pkg.{Class.method => alias}, and the body becomes alias(args), the
 * parameters in order, self first for a method of a trait or object (a dotted
 * method's self added, a functional method's moved to the front), as walk's
 * NativeMeth passes them.  Where the declaration gives an argument or the result
 * the type NN32, NN64 or Char (Character in the compiler's prelude), and the helper's
 * Java type there is an int or a long, which the checker reads as ZZ32 or ZZ64, that
 * argument or the call goes through the matching one of the six transfer helpers,
 * whose names the checker reads at the declared type (NamingCzar), as the prelude
 * composes them: makeNN32FromZZ32(unsignedIntOverflowingAdd(makeZZ32FromNN32(self),
 * makeZZ32FromNN32(b))); a position that the helper's own name already reads at the
 * declared type, as each transfer's, gets none.  A declaration with a varargs
 * parameter is left alone.
 * A string under the helpers' package that names no public static method is a
 * static error at the string.  Any other string is left alone, walk's glue classes
 * ("pkg.Class$Op") among them, so that its body stays a call of builtinPrimitive.
 *
 * Shell.specificRepository turns it on for the compiled path's repository and off
 * for walk's, which loads such a body itself.  Parser applies it to the parse of a
 * component (parseFileConvertExn) and to the import collector's view of a component
 * that names a helper (importCollector), so that the repository knows the foreign

It also names the package that defines the subclasses of the classes
\texttt{NativeFn0} to \texttt{NativeFn4}
\texttt{com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim}, where it said
\texttt{com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.primitive}, a package that the
implementation does not have.
The comment gains a box.
\item[Rationale] This change does not follow from route~A; it follows the
revival's decision of 10~October 2026 that every native binding of \library\
keeps the library's own form, a body that is exactly a call of
\VAR{builtinPrimitive}, and that its string names a static helper of the
package \texttt{com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers}, the compiled code's own
helpers, in place of a glue class, which takes the interpreter's values and
which the compiled code cannot call.
The bindings move onto helpers step by step, and the type checker checks each
moved binding against its helper's Java signature from the step that moves it.
The alternative not taken was \KWD{import} \KWD{java} declarations written in
the source files of \library, the compiler's own form for its natives, which
the interpreter does not run.
A reversal would restore the original comment, put the moved bindings back on
their glue classes, and leave the compiled code without a binding of the
natives of \library\ that it can call.
The full reasoning is in
\nolinkurl{explorations/compile-ladder/rung-natives-walk/decision-record.md}
in the revival's repository.
\item[Effect] Twenty-one of the 449 bindings of \library\ name a helper:
nineteen of the trait \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, its operators \EXP{=}, \EXP{<}, the
prefix and infix \EXP{-} and \EXP{\dotminus}, \EXP{+}, \EXP{\dotplus},
\EXP{\cdot}, \EXP{\times}, juxtaposition, \EXP{\dottimes}, \EXP{\div},
\OPR{BITAND}, \OPR{BITOR}, \OPR{BITXOR} and \OPR{BITNOT} and its functions
\VAR{widen} and \VAR{unsigned}, and the getters \VAR{asString} and
\VAR{asExprString} of the interpreter's object \TYP{Int}.
The other 428 still name a glue class, which the compiled code cannot call.
Among them is \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}'s \OPR{CHOOSE}: its helper throws a Java
\texttt{ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException}, which no \KWD{catch} sees, where the
binomial coefficient is past the helper's table, instead of an
\TYP{IntegerOverflow} (row~521 of the revival's gap ledger).
Until the compiled code moves onto \library, the type checker checks the moved
bindings, but no compiled program runs them.
Under the interpreter a helper's raise of \TYP{IntegerOverflow} or
\TYP{DivisionByZero} is the library's own exception, so \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}'s
\EXP{\div} by zero throws a \TYP{DivisionByZero}, as \chapref{operators} says of
an integer result; \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}'s \OPR{REM} and \OPR{MOD}, the three on
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}64}, and \EXP{\div} on \EXP{\mathbb{Z}}, which still name glue
classes, end the run with a Java exception at a divisor of zero (row~336 of
the revival's gap ledger), and so do \EXP{\div}, \OPR{REM} and \OPR{MOD} on
\EXP{\mathbb{N}32} and \EXP{\mathbb{N}64} and \OPR{REM} and \OPR{MOD} on
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}} (row~848 of the revival's gap ledger).
The interpreter passes a helper declared over \TYP{String}, as its glue classes
do, the name of the value's type in place of its characters where the value is
not a flat string, as a \TYP{String} made by concatenating two long strings
(row~846 of the revival's gap ledger).
The interpreter reads the \KWD{self} of a method only by the helper's Java
type, since it is not told the type that declares the method: a helper bound
in a method of a type that no Java type carries, as a program's own object,
is not refused, and its call passes the object as that Java type reads it,
the name of its type to a helper over \TYP{String} (row~847 of the
revival's gap ledger).
The compiler leaves a declaration with a varargs parameter as a call of
\VAR{builtinPrimitive}, so the type checker does not check such a binding
against its helper (row~849 of the revival's gap ledger); no binding of
\library\ that names a helper has a varargs parameter.
\item[Original text] The comment is typeset from the file
\nolinkurl{ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fsi} of the revival's
repository, lines 14--29, unchanged from the team's last commit until this

inputs a file \nolinkurl{library/apis/FortressBuiltin.tex} that the
specification's build typesets from that \apiN\ and that neither copy keeps.

content.content:
api FortressBuiltin

(** The %builtinPrimitive% function is actually recognized as a special piece
    of built-in magic by the Fortress interpreter and, where its argument names a helper, by the compiler.  The %javaClass%
    argument names either a glue class, a Java Class which is a subclass of
    \texttt{com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.NativeApp}, which provides code
    for the closure which is used in place of the call to
    %builtinPrimitive% and which only the interpreter runs, or a helper, a public static method of a Java class of the package \texttt{com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers}, written \texttt{com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.}\textit{Class}\texttt{.}\textit{method}, which both the interpreter and the compiled code call.  The interpreter loads a helper beside its glue classes: among the methods of that name it takes the one whose Java parameter and result types carry the declared types, %self% first, and it carries each value at its declared type.  The compiler, before type checking, rewrites the body into a call of the helper, which the type checker checks against the helper's Java signature.  A string under \texttt{com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers} that names no such method is an error on both.  Meanwhile all the necessary type information,
    argument names, etc. must be declared here in Fortress-land.  For examples, see the end of this file.
    \revision{revival-native-helpers}{The argument names a glue class, which only the interpreter runs, or a static helper of \texttt{com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers}, which both the interpreter and the compiled code call; and the package that defines the subclasses of the %NativeFn% classes is named as the implementation names it.}

    In practice, if you are extending the interpreter you will probably
    want to extend \texttt{com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.NativeFn0,1,2,3,4}
    or one of their subclasses defined in
    \texttt{com.sun.fortress.interpreter.glue.prim}.  These types are
    generally easier to work with, and the boilerplate packing and
    unpacking of values is done for you.
**)
builtinPrimitive[\T\](javaClass:String):T

#!/bin/bash
# Compile-path ladder, restricted to the files this rung can affect.
#
# A copy of ../run-ladder.sh with two changes: the ladder root and output
# directory are private to this worktree, and the two whole-corpus loops are
# replaced by one driven by subset.txt (corpus<TAB>file per line).
#
# Pushes every interpreter test program (ProjectFortress/tests/*.fss) and every
# file in ProjectFortress/not_working_library_tests/ through the compiler path
# unchanged and records how far each one gets.
#
# Reproduce:  bash explorations/compile-ladder/run-ladder.sh
# Outputs:    explorations/compile-ladder/raw/<corpus>/<name>.{compile,run}
#             explorations/compile-ladder/results.tsv
#
# The run uses a private cache tree so it never touches default_repository/caches
# (fortress.caches system property + FORTRESS_CACHES env; ProjectProperties.java:283,
# same mechanism the suite uses at build.xml:941-943), and a private java.io.tmpdir
# so the 5.8 MB Rats! temp directory of every grammar-importing run (RatsUtil.java:138-144)
# is swept per file instead of filling the disk.

set -u

source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../../explorations/experiment/env.sh"

LADDER_ROOT="${LADDER_ROOT:-$FORTRESS_HOME/tmp/ladder-r1}"
export LADDER_CACHES="$LADDER_ROOT/ladder-caches"
export LADDER_TMP="$LADDER_ROOT/ladder-tmp"
export FORTRESS_CACHES="$LADDER_CACHES"
export JAVA_FLAGS="-Xmx2g -Xss64m -Dfortress.caches=$LADDER_CACHES -Djava.io.tmpdir=$LADDER_TMP"

PRISTINE="$LADDER_ROOT/pristine"
OUT="$FORTRESS_HOME/explorations/compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static"
RAW="$OUT/raw"
TSV="$OUT/results.tsv"

COMPILE_TIMEOUT=120
RUN_TIMEOUT=60
MIN_FREE_KB=512000

mkdir -p "$RAW/tests" "$RAW/not_working_library_tests" "$LADDER_TMP"

disk_guard () {
    local free
    free=$(df -P / | awk 'NR==2{print $4}')
    if [ "$free" -lt "$MIN_FREE_KB" ]; then
        echo "STOP: only ${free} KB free on / (floor ${MIN_FREE_KB} KB)" | tee -a "$OUT/ladder.log"
        exit 2
    fi
    echo "-- disk free ${free} KB, cache $(du -sm "$LADDER_CACHES" | cut -f1) MB"
}

# Step 1: the compiler-world library, in the order repo-internals.md gives.
build_library () {
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || exit 1
    local f
    for f in LibraryBuiltin/AnyType.fss LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss \
             ../Library/CompilerLibrary.fss ../Library/CompilerAlgebra.fss \
             ../Library/CompilerSystem.fss ; do
        echo "library: $f"
        timeout 600 ../bin/fortress compile "$f" || { echo "LIBRARY BUILD FAILED on $f"; exit 1; }
    done
}

# Step 2: one known-good compiled program must print PASS before the ladder starts.
sanity () {
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || exit 1
    timeout 200 ../bin/fortress compile library_tests/Integer1.fss > /dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
    timeout 60 ../bin/fortress run Integer1 2>&1 | grep -q PASS
}

# Keep only the library's own cache entries; a program's entries are never reused.
prune_cache () {
    ( cd "$LADDER_CACHES" && find . -type f -print ) | sort > "$LADDER_TMP/.now"
    ( cd "$PRISTINE" && find . -type f -print ) | sort > "$LADDER_TMP/.keep"
    comm -23 "$LADDER_TMP/.now" "$LADDER_TMP/.keep" | while read -r p; do
        rm -f "$LADDER_CACHES/$p"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The gap ledger's tool: it owns the ledger's format, reads its rows, and is
the only way to write them.

The ledger, explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md, is sorted into topic sections,
each a "## TITLE" heading over one table of rows. A row is one line of eight
cells, and keeps its number wherever it sits:

  | # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |

The template (POSITIONS.md, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is
explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md, 4.1):
  status       exactly one of POSITIVE-VERIFIED, NEGATIVE-VERIFIED,
               NEGATIVE-BOUNDED, CONTESTED, RETIRED, FIXED, DUPLICATE
  class        `kind (area)`, kind one of the legend's seven, area one of ten;
               `—` only for POSITIVE-VERIFIED and RETIRED
  spec         the .tex file and the section heading in quotes; a line number
               only against Specification-1.0-frozen/; `silent` where the
               specification does not say
  reproducer   one test (a name under the test folders, or a path) or probe
               path from the repository root, or `none`
  limits       row 1,200 characters, claim 300, reproducer 200, found by 60,
               notes 700
  a pipe inside a cell is written \\|

Cells are split only at a pipe that is not escaped as \\|. A row whose cells
hold bare pipes (the ledger had six) does not split into its table's width that
way; it is read by its split at pipes followed by a space or the line's end, as
facts-extract.py has always read it, and check reports it under `pipe`.

Every write takes a lock (flock on .ledger.lock beside the ledger), checks the
template on the line it writes, and puts the full earlier line of a row it
changes, unchanged, in the history file beside the ledger
(fortress-gap-ledger-history.md), under "### Row N" and a line saying what
became of it. A failed check prints the rules the row breaks and exits 1.
add, rewrite, close and duplicate check the whole line they write; note checks
only what it changes (the notes cell and the row's length), so that a row
failing the template elsewhere still takes a note. A row at its length limit
takes no note: rewrite cuts it back (the rework's decision D4, "each is cut
when next edited", process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md).

usage: ledger.py COMMAND [ARGS] [--root DIR] [--ledger FILE] [--history FILE]

  heads                      one tab-separated line per row: number, status,
                             class, the claim's first 150 characters, and the
                             paths the row cites in backticks
  sections                   each section that holds a row table: its row
                             count and title, tab-separated
  section TITLE              the heads of that section's rows
  show N [--short]           row N under its section and table header; with
                             --short, its status, class, claim and the notes'
                             first 300 characters
  find WORDS [--open] [--cites FILE[:LINE]] [--all]
                             one line per row that holds every word (whole
                             words, or a word's start with a trailing *):
                             number, status, class, the claim's start; --open
                             leaves out FIXED, DUPLICATE and RETIRED; --cites
                             keeps the rows citing FILE (at LINE) and prints
                             the lines they cite; at most 10 rows unless --all
  count                      the rows by status, kind and area; nothing stored
  add FILE --section TITLE   FILE holds one row line, its # cell `?` (or the
                             seven cells after it); numbers it max + 1 and
                             inserts it in that section's table in number
                             order
  note N TEXT                adds TEXT to row N's notes, before the row's own
                             "full text: history, row N" marker where it has
                             one, else at their end (notes of `none` are
                             replaced); checks the notes cell and the row's
                             length only, so a failure in another cell does
                             not block it; a row keeps its own cells
  rewrite N FILE             FILE holds row N's whole new line (its # cell N
                             or ?, or the seven cells after it); checks it
                             against the template and writes it in the row's
                             place, its earlier line in the history
                             ("rewritten"): the route that corrects a claim,
                             cuts notes, or moves a reproducer. A FIXED or
                             DUPLICATE row stays so (a FIXED row's commit is
                             checked); a row becomes one only by close or
                             duplicate
  close N --commit HASH --test NAME [--settled TEXT] [--note TEXT] [--claim C]

component_of () {
    # component/api name as declared, which is what `fortress run` wants
    sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*\(component\|api\)[[:space:]]\+\([A-Za-z0-9_.]\+\).*/\2/p' "$1" | head -1
}

run_one () {
    local corpus="$1" path="$2"
    local base name comp crc rrc t0 t1 ct rt
    base=$(basename "$path")
    name="${base%.*}"
    comp=$(component_of "$path")
    [ -n "$comp" ] || comp="$name"

    t0=$(date +%s)
    timeout -k 5 "$COMPILE_TIMEOUT" ../bin/fortress compile "$path" \
        > "$RAW/$corpus/$base.compile" 2>&1
    crc=$?
    t1=$(date +%s); ct=$((t1-t0))

    rrc=""
    rt=""
    if [ "$crc" -eq 0 ] && [ "${base##*.}" = "fss" ]; then
        t0=$(date +%s)
        timeout -k 5 "$RUN_TIMEOUT" ../bin/fortress run "$comp" \
            > "$RAW/$corpus/$base.run" 2>&1
        rrc=$?
        t1=$(date +%s); rt=$((t1-t0))
    fi

    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' \
        "$corpus" "$base" "$comp" "$crc" "$rrc" "$ct" "$rt" >> "$TSV"
    echo "$corpus/$base crc=$crc rrc=$rrc ${ct}s"
}

main () {
    echo "=== ladder start $(date -Is) ==="
    disk_guard
    if [ ! -d "$PRISTINE" ]; then
        build_library
        rm -rf "$PRISTINE"; cp -a "$LADDER_CACHES" "$PRISTINE"
    fi
    sanity || { echo "SANITY FAILED: library_tests/Integer1 did not print PASS"; exit 1; }
    echo "sanity ok: library_tests/Integer1 compiles and prints PASS"
    prune_cache

    : > "$TSV"
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || exit 1

    local n=0 line corpus f
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r corpus f; do
        [ -n "$corpus" ] || continue
        run_one "$corpus" "$corpus/$f"
        n=$((n+1))
        rm -rf "${LADDER_TMP:?}"/fortress*rats
        if [ $((n % 10)) -eq 0 ]; then prune_cache; disk_guard; fi
    done < "$OUT/subset.txt"
    prune_cache
    echo "=== ladder done $(date -Is), $n files ==="
    disk_guard
}

main "$@"

## 1. What changed and why

P-58 has each native binding name a static helper of `nativeHelpers/`, checked against its helper from the step that moves it. For a binding over `NN32`, `NN64` or `Char`, walk already carries the declared type in a Java `int` or `long` (F-299), but the compiled checker reads every helper's `int` as `ZZ32` and `long` as `ZZ64`, except for six transfer helpers with fixed names (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/NamingCzar.java:367-391`, `:483-495`; F-298). - **The rewrite** (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/BuiltinPrimitiveRewriter.java`, +95 −12). Each declaration is told its owner, the simple name of the enclosing trait or object, `""` for a generic one, `null` at the top level (`:75`, `:91`). `fn` records each argument's declared type by its simple name, `self` taking the owner's (`:113-127`). Where the string names exactly one public static method of that name and arity (`soleMethod`, `:196-206`), each argument whose helper parameter is an `int` or a `long` that `NamingCzar.fortressTypeForForeignJavaType` reads otherwise than the declared `NN32`, `NN64` or `Char` (`Character` in the compiler's prelude) is wrapped in the matching transfer, and so is the call where the declared result type differs from the reading of the helper's result (`transfer`, `:176-193`; `:135-157`). A position the helper's own name already reads at the declared type, as each transfer's, gets none. So `opr +(self,b:NN32):NN32 = builtinPrimitive("…unsignedIntOverflowingAdd")` is checked and compiled as `makeNN32FromZZ32(unsignedIntOverflowingAdd(makeZZ32FromNN32(self), makeZZ32FromNN32(b)))`. content.content:
# Source this in every shell that runs Fortress:  source explorations/experiment/env.sh
export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64
export PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH"
export FORTRESS_HOME="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
unset JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS
export FORTRESS_THREADS=1
# bin/fortress defaults to -Xmx256m (gap ledger row 67); the checks at 4 threads override FORTRESS_THREADS on the command line
export JAVA_FLAGS="-Xmx4g -Xss64m"
# every grammar-importing run leaves a 5.8 MB Rats! temp directory behind (RatsUtil.getTempDir); 723 of them filled the disk allowance on 2026-09-15.
# Remove only those that no run can still be using: nothing in it written for an hour, and no java process now
# running started before its last write (a run makes its directory after it starts, and reads it until it ends).
(
  oldest=$(ps -C java -o etimes= 2>/dev/null | sort -n | tail -1 | tr -d ' ')
  now=$(date +%s)
  find /tmp -maxdepth 1 -type d -name 'fortress*rats' -mmin +60 -printf '%T@ %p\n' 2>/dev/null |
  while read -r t d ; do
    [ -n "$oldest" ] && [ "${t%.*}" -ge $(( now - oldest )) ] && continue
    [ -n "$(find "$d" -newermt '60 minutes ago' -print -quit 2>/dev/null)" ] && continue
    rm -rf "$d"
  done
)

What the tree now does: on the compiled path a `builtinPrimitive` body that names a helper is rewritten into that same composition wherever the declaration gives `NN32`, `NN64` or `Char` to a position that the helper's Java type carries in an `int` or a `long`, so the library's bare body, `opr +(self,b:NN32):NN32 = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleUnsignedIntArith.unsignedIntOverflowingAdd")`, checks and runs at its declared types (`ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/NativeHelperTransferCompiled`); 20 of `NN32`'s, 17 of `NN64`'s and 39 of `Char`'s bindings name their helpers, and under walk `NN32`'s and `NN64`'s `DIV` by zero throw `DivisionByZero`, where they ended the run (`ProjectFortress/tests/NN32DivisionByZeroWalk`, `NN64DivisionByZeroWalk`); walk's other values are the glue classes' (`ProjectFortress/tests/NativeHelperFamilyNN32Walk`, `NativeHelperFamilyNN64Walk`, `NativeHelperFamilyCharWalk`).
